name: Schumann 7.83 Hz sine
origin: Popular Schumann-resonance device concept (hypothesis: Cherry 2002); tested in an RCT by Huang et al. 2022 (Chang Gung, Taiwan)
summary: A 7.83 Hz sine for 30 min on all eight ring coils in phase, the popular 'Schumann resonance' relaxation and sleep program. Its health claims are hypotheses or vendor statements; the one RCT of a Schumann sleep device found no between-group difference on polysomnography.
notes: The natural Schumann resonance is a field of about 1 pT near 7.8 Hz (the fundamental drifts between about 7.2 and 8.2 Hz over the day); even at 1 uT the helmet is about a million times stronger, so this is not a 'natural' field. Cherry 2002 proposed health effects via melatonin as a hypothesis. Huang 2022 put a device by the bed facing the head, switched on about 1 h before bed until rising, for 4 weeks, with a composite 7.83 Hz plus theta and delta signal (this program plays only the 7.83 Hz part) and no reported field strength; polysomnography showed no between-group difference, and a co-author held the patent licence. Danho 2025 used 1 uT at 7.83 Hz (outcome: jump performance) with a no-exposure control but no sham. At about 1e-6 V/m induced field there is no credible mechanism. Treat it as claim-level and test it against sham with the app's Blind option. No sleep or health benefit is promised; stop on discomfort. The lowfield-schumann-783-harmonics program adds the higher resonance modes.
setting: Evening, lying down in a quiet, dim room; 30-60 min (Huang 2022 ran the device from about 1 h before bed until rising). All eight ring coils in phase, as there is no evidence-based placement.
source: Huang et al. 2022, Nat Sci Sleep https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35707548/ ; Einstein Telescope Schumann-resonance study, arXiv 2110.14730 (SR amplitude about 1 pT) https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.14730 ; Ouyang et al. 2013, Chinese J Geophys 56(3):265-272 (SR modes 7.8, 14.1, 20.3, 26.4, 32.5 Hz) https://html.rhhz.net/Geophy_en/html/20130304.htm ; Cherry 2002, Natural Hazards 26:279 https://ideas.repec.org/a/spr/nathaz/v26y2002i3p279-331.html ; Danho et al. 2025, Cureus https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41080364/
